title: Getting started with energese
text: symbol specific meaning Odum’s framework: Source (circle) — renewable external input system. Sun, wind, tide, hydrocarbon deposits, uranium. Generic flow (arrow) — energy flow components. Storage (Bertalanffy module — flat top, rounded bottom) — reservoir matter, energy, information. Named Ludwig von Bertalanffy, general-systems theorist. Consumer (hexagon) — entity uses stored emergy. Interaction (right-pointing chevron) — multiplicative junction two flows combine. Odum’s canonical shape chevron, diamond. Producer (rounded rectangle pointed right, aka “bullet”) — autocatalytic unit captures concentrates emergy. Plants, agriculture, power stations. Switch (bowtie) — /logic gate. Self-limiter (semi-circle) — producer/consumer whose output saturates. Heat sink / Energy Loss (-arrow ground) — dispersed heat end transformation. Every transformation eventually terminates heat sink per second law. Transaction (elongated diamond $ label) — money node, drawn money flow going opposite direction energy flow (dashed connecting lines).

title: Getting started with energese
text: Sun → producer (autotroph) → consumer (herbivore) → consumer (carnivore), heat-sink arrow ground:
code: library(ggplot2) library(energese)  nodes <- data.frame(   x    = c(1,   4,     7,          10),   y    = c(1.5, 1.5,   1.5,        1.5),   role = c("sun", "plant", "herbivore", "carnivore"))  ggplot() +   geom_odum_source  (data = nodes[1, ], aes(x = x, y = y),                      radius = 0.4, fill = "#F1C40F") +   geom_odum_producer(data = nodes[2, ], aes(x = x, y = y),                      width = 1.8, height = 1.0, fill = "#228B22") +   geom_odum_consumer(data = nodes[3, ], aes(x = x, y = y),                      width = 1.6, height = 1.0, fill = "#F39C12") +   geom_odum_consumer(data = nodes[4, ], aes(x = x, y = y),                      width = 1.6, height = 1.0, fill = "#C0392B") +   # Energy flows   geom_segment(aes(x = 1.5, xend = 3.0, y = 1.5, yend = 1.5),                arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.10, "in")),                linewidth = 0.6) +   geom_segment(aes(x = 4.9, xend = 6.2, y = 1.5, yend = 1.5),                arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.10, "in")),                linewidth = 0.6) +   geom_segment(aes(x = 7.8, xend = 9.2, y = 1.5, yend = 1.5),                arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.10, "in")),                linewidth = 0.6) +   # Heat sinks below each consumer   geom_odum_heat_sink(data = nodes[2:4, ],                      aes(x = x, y = y - title: ggplot2 Layers for H.T. Odum's Energy Systems Language
text: energese provides ggplot2 layers H.T. Odum’s Energy Systems Language (ESL) — also known Energese, Energy Circuit Language, Generic Systems Symbols — visual vocabulary ten canonical symbols Howard T. Odum developed 1950s tropical-forest studies El Verde, Puerto Rico (Odum & Pigeon 1970, funded U.S. Atomic Energy Commission) formalised later systems-ecology work. See Wikipedia article general introduction. Every canonical ESL symbol Wikipedia’s Energese reference chart exposed proper ggplot2 layer: takes standard ggplot2 aesthetics (x, y, fill, colour, alpha, linewidth) plus geometry aesthetic (width + height polygonal symbols, radius circular ones), vectorised rows data, composes naturally ggplot(), facet_*(), gganimate, patchwork, etc.

title: ggplot2 Layers for H.T. Odum's Energy Systems Language
text: hood geom_odum_* extends ggplot2::GeomPolygon uses internal .expand_odum() helper convert row data set polygon vertices, delegates rendering GeomPolygon. means every layer supports full ggplot2 grammar box — facets, animations, palettes, coordinate systems, statistical transformations. Symbols multiple sub-polygons (switch, heat_sink) emit sub-parts distinct group values outlines don’t self-cross. users want direct access polygon coordinates (e.g. gganimate transition_states non-ggplot renderers), low-level vertex helpers also exported: odum_circle(), odum_source(), odum_flow(), odum_storage(), odum_consumer(), odum_interaction(), odum_producer(), odum_switch(), odum_self_limiter(), odum_heat_sink(), odum_transaction(), odum_money().

title: ggplot2 Layers for H.T. Odum's Energy Systems Language
text: deep scan CRAN, GitHub, PyPI, biennial Emergy Synthesis proceedings found grammar--graphics ESL library. closest peers: EmSim (Valyi & Ortega 2004) — Java ODE integrator ESL diagrams, rendering API, effectively abandoned. sholtomaud/odum-energy-language — TypeScript GUI drag--drop editor, data binding. Sholto Maud also produced Visio stencil Wikipedia’s Energese chart based — chart package’s plot_energese_reference() reproduces programmatically. International Society Advancement Emergy Research — reference SVG images, programmatic stencils. energese fills gap: programmatic, data-bindable Odum ESL layers R’s grammar graphics.

title: ggplot2 Layers for H.T. Odum's Energy Systems Language
text: Odum’s ESL visual notation emergy accounting — body ecological-economics theory built : Transformity (sej/J) — accumulated solar-emergy embodied one joule product; measures energy quality. Empower (sej/time) — rate emergy flow system. Maximum empower principle — Odum’s proposed fourth thermodynamic law: systems self-organise maximise power intake dominate natural selection. Emergy hierarchy — ordering processes transformity, raw sunlight (1 sej/J) fuels, food, information. need compute quantities real fuel-mix household data, see sibling package emburdensynth, uses energese diagrams provides emergy pipeline.

title: energese: ggplot2 Layers for H.T. Odum's Energy Systems Language — energese-package
text: Every canonical symbol Wikipedia's Energese reference chart (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Energese.jpg) exposed: geom_odum_source()       — circle (renewable / external input) geom_odum_flow()         — bare arrow (generic flow) geom_odum_storage()      — Bertalanffy module geom_odum_consumer()     — hexagon (consumer) geom_odum_interaction()  — chevron (multiplicative junction) geom_odum_producer()     — bullet (autocatalytic producer) geom_odum_switch()       — bowtie (logic gate) geom_odum_self_limiter() — semi-circle (saturating unit) geom_odum_heat_sink()    — -arrow + ground line (heat sink) geom_odum_transaction()  — elongated diamond (money transaction) See plot_energese_reference() single function reproduces Wikipedia's canonical chart. Two APIs exposed: High-level (recommended) — ggplot2 Geoms , standard aesthetics. Vectorised data rows; composable ggplot() pipeline like ggplot2 layer. Low-level — vertex-tibble helpers (odum_symbols) return (x, y, id) coordinates suitable ggplot2::geom_polygon(). Use want hand-compose polygons, animate gganimate, render outside ggplot2.

title: Odum ESL vertex helpers — odum_symbols
text: Low-level tibble-returning functions compute polygon vertices H.T. Odum's Energy Systems Language (ESL) symbols. Used internally geom_odum_source() family; also exported users want hand-compose ggplot2::geom_polygon() layers, animate gganimate, render outside ggplot2. Two inputs enter flat left edge, one output exits pointed right. Odum's canonical "multiplicative junction" symbol — distinctly diamond (shape switch Odum's ESL). Odum's autocatalytic-unit symbol. silhouette storage rotated 90° right: flat left edge, straight top+bottom, semi-circular right end. Odum's /logic gate. Two triangles meeting central point, bounding-box (w, h). Odum's "self-limited" unit — represents producer/consumer whose output saturates. Returns data.frame TWO groups: -arrow polygon horizontal ground line separate row-set (id column distinguishes ). Users can render together single geom_polygon + geom_segment, use geom_odum_heat_sink() wraps . Money flows opposite direction energy Odum's ESL, symbol drawn dashed connection transacting unit. returned tibble diamond body; caller adds geom_segment(linetype="dashed") flow line text label "$". Wikipedia's chart shows lone right-pointing arrow. helper returns arrow polygon (shaft + triangular head) drawing geom_polygon; use geom_odum_flow() add inside ggplot pipeline.

title: energese 0.1.0
text: First R grammar--graphics library H.T. Odum’s Energy Systems Language (ESL) — also known Energese. 10 exported ggproto Geoms matching Wikipedia’s canonical Energese reference chart (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Energese.jpg): geom_odum_source(), geom_odum_flow(), geom_odum_storage() (Bertalanffy module), geom_odum_consumer(), geom_odum_interaction() (chevron), geom_odum_producer() (bullet), geom_odum_switch() (bowtie), geom_odum_self_limiter() (semi-circle), geom_odum_heat_sink() (arrow + ground line), geom_odum_transaction() (elongated diamond). Matching low-level odum_* vertex-tibble helpers direct geom_polygon() composition non-ggplot renderers. plot_energese_reference() — reproduces Wikipedia’s Energese chart directly R. Vignette worked examples: symbol legend, simple ecosystem, interaction junction, small economic system money transaction. README + inst/CITATION canonical Odum + Brown references. Prior-art scan: author’s knowledge, first R (Python) grammar--graphics ESL library.
